blocking_findings: F26 [Blocker] review-a: The chibi row moves paragraph 1 out of the .article-text element (primary_template.html:1694-1712; paragraphs 2+ stay in .article-text at :1734). Paragraph 1 therefore loses the print rule .article-text { font-size: 12pt; line-height: 2 } (template :1387-1390) and takes the body line height 1.65 (template :1381-1384). Ghostscript txtwrite on the r10 PDFs measures a 19-21 pt line pitch for paragraph 1 on page 3 and a 24 pt pitch for paragraph 2 on page 4, in both proofs (Adventure 9.2 and Quest 5). So the first paragraph prints visibly tighter than the rest of the article. At S5.G6 and in the classic look, every paragraph prints at line height 2. The Red test checks only the markup order and the grid display, so no test catches this. Fix: give paragraph 1 the .article-text print size and line height inside the row (for example an article-text wrapper in the right column, or one chibi rule), add a test that compares the winning line-height of paragraph 1 and paragraph 2 in the chibi render, and rerun the proof (P14, P17, P20). Rationale: a defect in the remediation lines that changes the printed article for the child reader.

F27 [Major] review-a: The marking key moved. The chibi branch prints the .marking-legend after the row, so the key now sits between paragraph 1 and paragraph 2 (primary_template.html:1715; r10 print HTML offsets: row 935729, legend 936901, article-text 938328). The classic branch and S5.G6 print the key before paragraph 1 (template :1778; the template CSS comment at :1504 says 'Marking key under the QR box'). On the r10 Adventure 9.2 page 3 the key prints under the hero caption, after the student reads paragraph 1. The PM option B decision covers the hero and paragraph 1 only, not the key. Fix: render the legend before the row, as in the classic order, or record a PM decision for the new place. Route: Green.

F28 [Major] review-a: Production CSS is changed to satisfy a test helper. workbook-document-wrapper.ts:28-31 rewrites every 'chibi-hero-row' in the chibi stylesheet to the escape '\63 hibi-hero-row', with the comment that the page-flow guard finds the row by the first occurrence of the class name. The cause is extractRow at chibi-quest-page-flow.test.ts:115, which uses html.indexOf('chibi-hero-row') and so finds the CSS selector in the head first. The escape is valid CSS, and P14 and P20 prove the layout on r10. But the wrapper now carries a string rewrite that exists only for one test, and any future chibi rule that names the class gets the same rewrite. Fix: the test author changes extractRow to find class="chibi-hero-row" in the markup; then Green removes the replaceAll call. Route: Red, then Green.

F29 [Nit] review-a: The row carries break-inside: avoid and wraps the hero area (chibi-quest-styles.ts:117-118). The comment at chibi-quest-styles.ts:97-98 says the hero wrappers must not carry this rule because Paged.js dropped a tall hero area (P11, round 2). P11 passes on the two r10 proofs (3 of 3 pictures each), so the current proofs are safe. A lesson with a taller row moves the whole row to the next page and can leave the step 3 header and QR box alone; only two lessons prove the rule. Fix: update the comment so it states why the row may carry the keep rule, and name the residual risk in test-strategy.md. Route: Green for the comment, the plan author for the strategy.
